public_rationale: Before the post, OpenAI's CEO confirmed that licensed Shutterstock data had been used to train DALL-E, and OpenAI disclosed licensed content among ChatGPT's training sources. The contemporaneous CRS report also records OpenAI's acknowledged use of copyrighted datasets. Together, these records support the factual claim. Licensing does not remove copyright protection, so authorized use counts.
limitations: The records do not provide a complete inventory of training works or establish which material entered every model version.
This assessment does not determine whether any training use infringed copyright.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI systems such as DALL-E and ChatGPT were trained on copyrighted materials.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI systems like DALL-E and ChatGPT have been trained on copyrighted materials;
statement.document_title: Things are about to get a lot worse for Generative AI

from_speaker: Generative AI systems like DALL-E and ChatGPT
our_interpretation: This concerns training completed before publication, including earlier versions of the named product families.
The post specifies no beginning date for that historical training, so the target period has an open start and ends on December 29, 2023.
Copyrighted materials includes licensed material. The claim does not require that the training was unauthorized or unlawful.
Both named product families must be covered; evidence about an unrelated model alone would not suffice.
criteria.support_condition: Company disclosures or reliable training records establish that copyrighted material was included in training DALL-E and models serving ChatGPT before the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records establish that a named product family was trained entirely without copyrighted material, for example solely on public-domain or otherwise unprotected data.
